trust_decision.summary: The number of trailing/empty line breaks in a STRIP or CLIP block scalar (document-controlled) decides how much stack fy_atom_iter_format() takes. Each doubling of the pending line-break buffer uses alloca() inside the per-line loop, so the stack grows with input size and is never bounded or moved to the heap.

landing_point.why: The advisory names fy_atom_iter_format() and block scalars. The only alloca() calls in the function are at src/lib/fy-atom.c:1045 and :1067, both inside the STRIP/CLIP block.

fix_sites.module_kind: core library, atom text formatter (declarations: in-place buffer + heap pointer)

fix_sites.entry_point: same: any public API that formats a block-scalar token's text

O3_reason_to_dismiss: fy-parse.c:1201 sizes an alloca() from the formatted text length of a document-bottom comment, a different allocation in another file. It runs only when FYPCF_PARSE_COMMENTS is set (src/lib/fy-parse.c:6644), so a solver can call it a non-default comment feature that has nothing to do with block scalars.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: CLIP chomping must still emit exactly one final line break (pending_lb[0]), and interior empty lines must keep their actual line-break character (actual_lb, e.g. CRLF), not a hard-coded '\n'. A fix that drops or caps the pending breaks changes scalar content. The fix's own test compares the exact text of a 4096-empty-line literal.

O6_input_shapes: manual literal/folded styles (fy_atom_style_is_block masks FYAS_MANUAL_MARK, src/lib/fy-atom.h:53-57)
empty lines with non-'\n' line breaks (actual_lb)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Bottom-of-document comment text is formatted into a stack buffer of alloca(length+1), where length is the input-controlled comment length (needs FYPCF_PARSE_COMMENTS)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different function and file, only with the comment-parsing flag, a one-off rather than per-line alloca, and it does not go through the block-scalar pending buffer
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file, same package (src/lib/fy-parse.c vs src/lib/fy-atom.c)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the trailing_breaks loop for flow/quoted scalars could realistically buffer the breaks in a growing alloca array like the block path does
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same function already uses this buffering idiom for block scalars, so a maintainer could copy it to the quoted-scalar last-line path

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the KEEP chomp branch could buffer pending breaks the same way (today it emits them directly)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A refactor that unified STRIP/CLIP/KEEP handling would naturally share the pending_lb buffer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: emitter indentation buffer is alloca(indent - column); a per-line loop variant would repeat the pattern on the output side
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The emitter already uses alloca for input-derived whitespace runs

O9_family: uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-770): stack exhaustion from alloca() inside an input-driven loop

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C compiler (GCC/Clang); optional libclang for reflection, check-style test harness under test/
O10_build.project_tests: test/libfyaml-test-core.c (alloca_check near the fix insertion point, fix.diff:70-72), plus YAML test-suite based tests; ENABLE_NETWORK option gates network tests (CMakeLists.txt:140)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the alloca() calls with a fixed-size array or a cap on pending_nl, which silently drops or corrupts long runs of empty lines; or switch to malloc and leak on the goto out paths

src/lib/fy-doc.c:4140-4149: node-walk ctx alloca sized by max_depth; a different subsystem, not pursued
